title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-03-21
lineage: Sony dynamic mics (balcony, 20' spread) > Sony 124 Cassette Deck > Norelco 120 normal bias tape > Susie Q > Tascam 122mk3 > Lucid ADA1000 A/D Converter > Tascam CDRW700 > EAC > Soundforge > CD Wave > mkwACT > SHN

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy early‑70s audience tape that captures a blistering Viola Lee Blues and other classics with surprisingly clear sound.
ai_review.review: The recording, sourced from an audience feed, sounds remarkably vivid for its era—many reviewers call it the best‑sounding AUD source of 1970. Musically the show shines thanks to a scorching Viola Lee Blues, raucous Walkin’ The Dog and rare jams like Seven and Cumberland, with Jerry’s psychedelic blues guitar drawing particular praise.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews overwhelmingly highlight strong performance (especially Viola Lee Blues) and a surprisingly good audience recording, with only minor complaints about occasional tape quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Listeners repeatedly note the tape sounds ‘nice’, ‘vintage’ and almost like it was recorded yesterday; a few mention occasional drop‑outs or that the recording isn’t perfect, but overall clarity is high for an early‑70s audience source.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The early show is praised for its informal, high‑energy vibe; the set flows through classic early‑70s material with rare jams that keep the momentum and audience interaction lively.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight Jerry’s primal psychedelic blues playing and his intense guitar tone on Viola Lee Blues.
